# Colony History
[italic]A short history of Fort McNeil for new arrivals, as the Herald's archive tells it.[/italic]
## A Border World White Antre sits on the edge of United Americas space in the Neroid Sector, close enough to the line that the comms crews hear foreign traffic on a quiet night. The surveyors rated it hot, dry and empty, with good ore under the rock and not much else. That was enough.
## The Fort The first drill crews came down with a landing pad, a generator and a ring of cargo modules stacked against the wind. Somebody called the camp the fort, the name stuck, and the survey office added McNeil to make it official. Nobody at the press office has ever found out who McNeil was.
## The Drill Sites - Fort McNeil lives on its drills. The northern, northeastern and southern sites run around the clock, and the Drill Coordination Module sets every shift. - Under the colony lies a maze of caves. Miners use them as shortcuts between the sites, and every year a few people go in further than they should. The old smuggler route past the colony is officially closed and unofficially busy. - Hydroponics grows most of the fresh food. Everything else comes in by the landing zone, when it comes.
## Keeping Order Colonial Security is small, underpaid and fond of donuts. Residents call the officers [bold]Bucketheads[/bold] after their helmets. They answer to Administration, and Administration answers to the people who own the drills.
## The Union Question Every few months union slips turn up in the dormitory and the mess. Every few months management takes them down. The miners want safer shafts, honest pay and a say in lockdowns. Management wants the quota met. The Herald prints both sides and lets the reader count the injuries.
## Weather White Antre is dry country. What passes for rain is a thin drizzle that the dust drinks before it can pool, and the wind keeps the grit moving the rest of the time. The atmospheric console in the colony has been set to forecast rain, and nothing but rain, for as long as anyone remembers. Nobody has the access code to change it, and residents call it the only forecast on White Antre that is never wrong.
The Herald keeps the archive so that nobody here gets written out of the record.
